To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) new digital media are not necessarily deregulatory; (b) new digital media do not automatically lead to the demise of the music industry; and (c) the recording industry is not necessarily doomed.
there is a global network of sharing and distribution that has been bypassed by the recording industry.

new technologies of music distribution and new legal frameworks for regulating music distribution do not determine the future of music distribution. Rather, the balance of social and political forces will determine the future of the music industry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the new digital technologies of the Internet, the Web, and digital media have been interpreted and re-interpreted in the context of the global music industry.
the way in which music audiences are located and relocated in the context of globalization.
the ways in which the global and the local, the public and the private, and the virtual and the real are mutually constituted and reconstituted.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the future is open and unpredictable.
the future will be determined by the balance of power between those who want to use new media to make a profit and those who want to share it freely.
there is no technical solution to social problems, that the law is always a social construction, and that the law is not the only social construction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new technologies are not so new after all.
the legal and the technical are both necessary but not sufficient to determine the future of music and the music business.

the global electronic network has the potential of being a new social space for the production and distribution of culture and the creation of new social relationships, but that it is also subject to appropriation and control by corporate and state interests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the law, technology and social relations are all implicated in the struggle over the ownership and use of music and other creative works.
we need a better understanding of the relationship between the social and technical dimensions of the digital economy.
the global is not an external, inevitable process but a set of practices that are enacted by a variety of actors.
